svg.aria-label: Fig. C3 System level cache: 8 MiB, 16 ways, 4096 sets, memory side, fully hashed
svg.text: Fig. C3 System level cache: 8 MiB, 16 ways, 4096 sets, memory side, fully hashed
Not a CPU cache in the usual sense. It sits on the memory side of coherence, holds what the L2s evict, and is exclusive of them.
every index bit is a hash
hash input: bits 32:7, each of the 12 index bits is an XOR of several of these (SLAC)
4096 sets x 16 ways x 128 B = 8 MiB (confirmed ways and size). The hash spreads addresses nearly evenly, so no stride crowds a few sets; the tag must then hold every bit the hash consumed.
duplicate L2 tags of every cluster, orders same address requests (patent, inferred)
memory side: a write that reaches it counts as written to DRAM (inferred)
fills from L2 victims; a CPU miss does not allocate (measured, two labs)
exclusive of the CPU caches: a line taken back by a CPU leaves at once (measured)
91 ns loaded; 68 GB/s peak; one core draws 64
misses and write backs; a DRAM read may start alongside the lookup, killed on a hit (patent)
one SLC line (field set from patents, widths mine)
state: only invalid, valid and modified; st: sticky. Only I, V, M: no shared or owned state, because nothing above it needs to be snooped
through it. Partial writes keep a byte mask; later designs track dirty per 64 B half (Handley v8).
group id and sticky: driver set quotas cap each client group, and replacement skips sticky lines (patent).
Range registers can map an address range into SLC lines as memory, for camera or display frames (patent).
Replacement: pseudo random (EXAM) against LRU placed by GPU reads (SLAC). Disputed. Proposed reconciliation:
the insertion position depends on the client group, so a CPU victim and a GPU read land in different LRU
positions and a probe from one side sees a different policy from a probe on the other.
Slices: two (even and odd lines, 2012 patent) or four planes (Asahi, documented). Each behind its own arbiter.
Latency about 90 cycles from a core (reported, no measurement pinned). Proposed split: 17 L2 miss detect,
20 to the coherence point and tag check, 30 SLC array at a lower clock, 20 return over the fabric.
Test: a pointer chase sized between 12 and 20 MiB gives the SLC latency directly once the L2 is
thrashed; nobody has published that number for the M1 with the chase confined to L2 victims.
Power: ways power down to match the share in use, idle SRAM held at retention voltage, low QoS
all 12 index bits hashed from PA 32:7
128 B, with per sector valid and a byte mask (patent)
pseudo random (EXAM) vs LRU for GPU placed lines (SLAC)
write back toward DRAM; memory side, so a write reaching it is architecturally done
exclusive of the CPU caches; filled by L2 victims and GPU reads
group quotas, sticky lines, address ranges mapped as memory
